# Calculate the growth ratio from the bar chart data

# Children's Books (orange) bounding boxes [x1, y1, x2, y2]
# Format: [x1, y1, x2, y2] where y1 is the top of the bar and y2 is the bottom (baseline)
children_books_bboxes = [
    [124, 289, 135, 892],  # 2013
    [198, 250, 209, 892],  # 2014
    [272, 229, 282, 892],  # 2015
    [345, 209, 356, 892],  # 2016
    [419, 189, 430, 892],  # 2017
    [493, 168, 503, 892],  # 2018
    [566, 148, 577, 892],  # 2019
    [640, 128, 650, 892],  # 2020
    [713, 108, 724, 892],  # 2021
    [787, 89, 798, 892],   # 2022
]

# Poetry (green) bounding boxes
poetry_bboxes = [
    [114, 732, 124, 892],  # 2013
    [187, 712, 197, 892],  # 2014
    [261, 692, 271, 892],  # 2015
    [334, 671, 344, 892],  # 2016
    [408, 651, 418, 892],  # 2017
    [482, 631, 492, 892],  # 2018
    [555, 611, 565, 892],  # 2019
    [629, 592, 639, 892],  # 2020
    [703, 571, 712, 892],  # 2021
    [776, 551, 786, 892],  # 2022
]

# Academic Texts (pink) bounding boxes
academic_bboxes = [
    [136, 611, 146, 892],  # 2013
    [209, 592, 219, 892],  # 2014
    [283, 571, 293, 892],  # 2015
    [357, 551, 367, 892],  # 2016
    [430, 531, 440, 892],  # 2017
    [503, 511, 514, 892],  # 2018
    [577, 490, 588, 892],  # 2019
    [651, 470, 661, 892],  # 2020
    [724, 450, 735, 892],  # 2021
    [798, 431, 808, 892],  # 2022
]

# Calculate bar heights (baseline is at y=892)
baseline = 892

# Children's Books heights
cb_2013_height = baseline - children_books_bboxes[0][1]  # 892 - 289 = 603
cb_2022_height = baseline - children_books_bboxes[9][1]  # 892 - 89 = 803

# Poetry heights
poetry_2013_height = baseline - poetry_bboxes[0][1]  # 892 - 732 = 160
poetry_2022_height = baseline - poetry_bboxes[9][1]  # 892 - 551 = 341

# Academic Texts heights
academic_2013_height = baseline - academic_bboxes[0][1]  # 892 - 611 = 281
academic_2022_height = baseline - academic_bboxes[9][1]  # 892 - 431 = 461

print(f"Children's Books 2013 height: {cb_2013_height} pixels")
print(f"Children's Books 2022 height: {cb_2022_height} pixels")
print(f"Poetry 2013 height: {poetry_2013_height} pixels")
print(f"Poetry 2022 height: {poetry_2022_height} pixels")
print(f"Academic 2013 height: {academic_2013_height} pixels")
print(f"Academic 2022 height: {academic_2022_height} pixels")

# Calculate growth in pixels
cb_growth_pixels = cb_2022_height - cb_2013_height
poetry_growth_pixels = poetry_2022_height - poetry_2013_height
academic_growth_pixels = academic_2022_height - academic_2013_height

print(f"\nChildren's Books growth: {cb_growth_pixels} pixels")
print(f"Poetry growth: {poetry_growth_pixels} pixels")
print(f"Academic growth: {academic_growth_pixels} pixels")

# Combined growth of Poetry and Academic
combined_growth_pixels = poetry_growth_pixels + academic_growth_pixels
print(f"Combined Poetry + Academic growth: {combined_growth_pixels} pixels")

# Now I need to find the scale factor (pixels per unit)
# Looking at the chart, the y-axis goes from 0 to 200+
# Let me estimate based on visual inspection:
# Children's Books 2013 appears to be at 150, 2022 at 200
# So 603 pixels ≈ 150 units, 803 pixels ≈ 200 units

# Let's calculate the scale factor
# If 603 pixels = 150 units, then scale = 150/603 = 0.2488 units/pixel
# If 803 pixels = 200 units, then scale = 200/803 = 0.2491 units/pixel
# Average: ~0.249 units/pixel

scale_factor = 200 / 803  # Using 2022 Children's Books as reference
print(f"\nScale factor: {scale_factor} units/pixel")

# Convert growth to actual values
cb_growth = cb_growth_pixels * scale_factor
poetry_growth = poetry_growth_pixels * scale_factor
academic_growth = academic_growth_pixels * scale_factor
combined_growth = combined_growth_pixels * scale_factor

print(f"\nChildren's Books growth: {cb_growth:.2f} units")
print(f"Poetry growth: {poetry_growth:.2f} units")
print(f"Academic growth: {academic_growth:.2f} units")
print(f"Combined Poetry + Academic growth: {combined_growth:.2f} units")

# Calculate the ratio
ratio = cb_growth / combined_growth
print(f"\nRatio (Children's Books growth / Combined Poetry + Academic growth): {ratio:.4f}")
print(f"Ratio as fraction: {cb_growth_pixels}/{combined_growth_pixels} = {cb_growth_pixels/combined_growth_pixels:.4f}")
